maya: Heads-up — ran a focused benchmark for prefill‑dominant longtail mix on staging-G4 last night. Numbers look inconsistent with our synthetic runs.
kevin: Which harness did you use, replay or synthetic?
maya: Replay harness using a 10% sampled production capture (24h). Prefills account for ~72% of token work; long tails out to 32k tokens. Kernel selection flips at 2k/4k boundaries and we saw a burst of kernel-swap events.
samir: Can you paste the perf summary/logs?
perf-bot: [auto-summary] run_id=2003456-1 avg_token_latency.p50=18.3ms p95=62.7ms kernel_swap_count=1340 avg_batch=3.2 kv_hit_rate=0.57 prefill_coverage=0.84
rachel: kv_hit_rate ~0.57 seems low for a prefill-heavy workload. Were prefix caches enabled for that run?
maya: No — I purposely disabled prefix/KV warmers to measure cold-chain behavior. Synthetic runs had warmers on by default; that likely explains most of the gap.
kevin: Ok — we need explicit apples‑to‑apples and realistic configs. Proposed matrix: (A) replay w/ no cache (realistic cold), (B) replay w/ prefix cache (apples-to-apples), (C) synthetic longmix (warm). All with kernel dump and identical drivers.
rachel: Also capture batching heuristic state — dynamic_batcher switched to conservative mode during swap storms which collapsed batch sizes to 1‑2. Snippet:```dynamic_batcher:
  min_batch: 1
  max_batch: 8
  swap_cooldown_ms: 120
```
samir: swap_cooldown_ms=120ms is aggressive for long-context runs. If kernel churn happens, cooldown encourages frequent swaps. Suggest raising to 500ms for longmix experiments.
maya: I collected syscall traces and kernel-dump logs — gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/perf/prefill-longtail (placeholder). Also microtrace for KV lookup latencies: misses tail at ~2.3ms.
kevin: If miss penalty > batching window, miss latencies will amplify p95. Consider prefetching the top-K context keys for heavy-prefill traces.
perf-bot: queued jobs: x-1201 (replay-no-cache), x-1202 (replay-with-cache), x-1203 (synthetic-longmix).
rachel: One more gotcha — hardware/driver mismatch. Last synthetic run used CUDA 12.2 while the replay baseline used 12.1. We must pin driver/kernel lib across runs for apples-to-apples.
maya: Agreed. I'll pin to CUDA 12.1 and the same cuDNN / kernel-lib build.
samir: Also add KV lookup histograms and batch size distribution to the CSV output. We want columns: run_id, gpu, driver, model_hash, p50_token, p95_token, avg_batch, kernel_swap_count, kv_hit_rate, kv_miss_p50, kv_miss_p95, tokens_per_sec.
kevin: When comparing runs, we should flag two classes of regressions: throughput regressions (tokens/sec) and latency regressions (p95). Synthetic often shows optimistic throughput because it yields larger batches; don't gate on synthetic alone.
maya: Quick note — synthetic had avg_batch=5.8 and better tokens/sec, but p95 for short queries increased because the large-kernel path has a higher cold tail. That skews ROC for regressions if we only look at tokens/sec.
rachel: PR plan: add perf harness templates that: 1) pin drivers, 2) control prefix cache on/off, 3) set swap_cooldown_ms, 4) enable kernel-dump, 5) emit KV microtraces. I'll open the PR in perf repo after we converge.
kevin: TL;DR: For regression gating use replay w/ apples-to-apples settings (prefix cache on + pinned drivers). Use replay-no-cache for realistic production risk estimates. Keep synthetic for debugging and microbench comparisons only.
samir: I'll run the three jobs tomorrow AM, collect CSVs, and run the apples-to-apples diff script. Will post results here.
maya: Thanks — small ask: are folks ok with setting swap_cooldown_ms to 500ms for the apples-to-apples runs? :thinking:
kevin: +1 :thumbsup:
rachel: +1

maya: Dropping a short checklist in the perf PR: ensure driver pin, caching mode, swap_cooldown, kernel-dump flag, kv-hist output. Will follow up with the CSV diffs once samir posts them.
kevin: Perfect. If we still see unexplained swap spikes after those controls, we should flip kernel selection logs into debug and repro a minimal trace.
samir: Copy — will attach debug dump if needed.
maya: Thanks all, closing loop after job results.
